title: Floot vs Bolt: Which AI App Builder Is Better in 2026?
summary: Floot's connector has your own Claude or ChatGPT account do the building, so there's no second AI bill; Bolt stays a fast, vendor-billed in-browser prototy…
body_markdown:
## What Is Floot?


Floot is primarily a **connector you add to ChatGPT or Claude** — you build your app by talking to the AI assistant you already use, in the app you already use. Floot also has its own in-app editor and its own AI agent, a fine way to work if you'd rather not leave Floot.


Either way you build, Floot handles the same backend: hosting, a real Postgres database, auth, serverless endpoints, custom domains, and publishing to the web, with mobile app conversion available on the Power plan.


## What Is Bolt?


Bolt is an AI-powered app builder focused on fast, in-browser front-end generation. You describe a UI in natural language and Bolt builds it inside its StackBlitz-powered environment, prompt to preview in seconds — a genuinely strong choice for rapid prototyping and concept validation.


Bolt has also shipped "Connectors," which let it pull live context from external tools while you work — Notion, Linear, GitHub, Miro, Sentry, and others. Whether Bolt can, in turn, be driven from inside Claude or ChatGPT the way Floot can isn't something we could confirm, so we're not claiming it either way here.


## Floot vs Bolt: Feature Comparison


### 1. Where you build


**Floot** — from inside ChatGPT or Claude, or from Floot's own editor and agent.


**Bolt** — inside Bolt's own browser-based environment; Connectors let it reach out to your other tools, but the building itself happens on bolt.new.


### 2. How you pay for the AI


**Floot** — you bring your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription. Floot's connector exposes primitives — read and write files, run SQL, typecheck, deploy — and your own assistant does the reasoning and writes the code. There's no second agent in the loop, so no second AI bill: the work is billed by Anthropic or OpenAI directly, at their price. What Floot charges for instead is **actions** (any edit, read, or test your assistant runs against your project — failed actions never count) and hosting.


**Bolt** — vendor-billed. You pay Bolt/StackBlitz a subscription that bundles a token allowance, with a free tier and paid tiers above it that raise the allowance and remove the daily cap; team pricing is billed per member. No bring-your-own-key option is offered.


Floot's actions and Bolt's token allowance are both charges on top of the Claude or ChatGPT subscription you already pay for, but the shape differs: Floot's actions reset daily and a failed action never counts, so worst case you're building again tomorrow. Bolt's token allowance is a balance you draw down against your plan — we can't confirm exactly how or when it resets, but the basic shape is a pool you deplete rather than a ceiling that clears daily.


Across this category, a connector into Claude or ChatGPT is often a remote control for the vendor's own agent — your prompt gets forwarded, their agent builds on their infrastructure, and their credits get spent on top of what you already pay for the subscription. We can document that pattern for some competitors, but not for Bolt specifically: we found evidence that Bolt *calls out* to external MCP servers through Connectors, but no documentation that Bolt.new itself exposes an MCP server that Claude or ChatGPT could drive — so verify against Bolt's own docs if that matters to you.


One consequence of Floot's shape holds regardless of what Bolt does: because your own assistant is doing the building, whatever else is in that session — a Figma connector, other tools, files you've uploaded, instructions you've already given it — is available to it while it works.


### 3. Production readiness


Both platforms host what you build. Floot adds a managed Postgres database, auth, and serverless endpoints as standard, plus mobile app conversion on Power (app store publishing still needs your own Apple/Google developer accounts, and iOS builds need Xcode on a Mac). Bolt is strongest as a front-end and prototyping layer — check what's included on your plan versus what you'd wire up yourself for a production backend.


## Floot pricing


Floot has a free tier and paid tiers above it, with higher tiers adding custom domains, badge removal, priority support, and, on the top tier, mobile app conversion. Actions and credits are two separate meters: actions cover the building work itself, credits cover AI features running inside your finished app, or building with Floot's own agent instead of your own AI account.


## Is Floot a Bolt alternative?


If you already live in Claude or ChatGPT and want your own assistant to do the actual building — with no second agent or second AI bill stacked on your subscription — Floot is built for that. If your priority is the fastest possible in-browser front-end prototype and you're comfortable paying Bolt directly for tokens, Bolt remains a solid choice for that job.

## Final verdict: Floot vs Bolt in 2026


Bolt is genuinely good at fast, in-browser UI prototyping, and its Connectors make it easy to pull in context from the rest of your stack — a real strength, distinct from what Floot does. Floot's bet is different: your own assistant does the reasoning and writes the code, so building costs the subscription you already pay, plus Floot's actions-and-hosting meter, nothing more.
